title.narrative: UNDP - Funding Facility for Stabilization Irak 2018 - 2023
UNDP - Funding Facility for Stabilization Iraq 2018 - 2023 - UNDP FFS Iraq 2018 (Ny strategi 2022)

description.narrative:
The Funding Facility for Stabilization (FFS) consists of two channels of support, the original Funding Facility for Immediate Stabilisation (FFIS) and the more recently established channel Funding Facility for Expanded Stabilisation (FFES).
The FFS aim at immediate stabilisation and recovery measures in the liberated areas of IS control, in order for sustainable return of internally displaced persons (IDP) back to these areas (focus four governorat; Anbar, Salah al-Din, Diyala, Nineweh including east and west Mosul).

UNDP Funding Facility for Stabilization(FFS) avser att stödja den irakiska regeringens stabiliserings- och återuppbyggnadsbehov i de återtagna områdena, tidigare under IS kontroll, för att bidra till ett säkert och hållbart återvändande av internflyktingar till dessa områden (fokus fyra governorat; Anbar, Salah al-Din, Diyala, Nineweh, som inkluderar östra och västra Mosul).
Faciliteten etablerades av UNDP i dialog med den irakiska regeringen 2015, med stöd från givarsamhället, på grund av den pågående militära konflikten med IS, med omfattande strömmar av internflyktingar och humanitär kris som följd i stora delar av Irak.
Faciliteten är den enda i sitt slag i Irak som verkar så brett inom området för stabilisering och tidig återuppbyggnad och kompletterar det internationella humanitära stödet som annars är det mest omfattande i Irak. Sverige var ett av de drivande länderna för fondfacilitetens tillkomst, och stöd till UNDP har getts av Sverige via UD sedan 2015. Idag samlar fondfaciliteten 24 givarländer, där Sverige fortfarande är en av de största givarna.
Faciliteten består av två kanaler för stöd, Funding Facilitiy for Immediate Stabilization (FFIS) och fr o m 2016 också Funding Facility for Expanding Stabilization (FFES). Den första kanalen fokuserar på stöd till reparation av lätt infrastruktur som kan bidra till att få igång basala samhällstjänster inom sektorer som bl a vatten, el, avlopp, hälsa och utbildning samt kapacitetsstärkande stöd till lokala myndigheter. Det kompletteras med olika komponenter av försörjningsstöd (t ex cash-for work schemes) till utsatta grupper, som återvändande internflyktingar och kvinnoledda hushåll, samt finansiella bidrag till privata näringsidkare som kan bidra till att få igång det lokala näringslivet samt stöd till social sammanhållning (fredsbyggande mellan olika grupper). Programmet bidrar till att bygga resiliens i dessa utsatta lokalsamhällen.
Därutöver kompletteras faciliteten med en andra kanal, FFES, för att möta behovet av stöd till återuppbyggnad av mer omfattande infrastruktur, som t ex rehabilitering av sjukhusbyggnader, universitet, samt rehabilitering av objekt som broar och vägar som i sin tur bidrar till att upprätta stabiliseringskorridorer mellan återtagna områden och städer.
Den preliminära budgeten för hela faciliteten fram till 2023 är 1 880 000 000 USD.

The Government of Iraq is supported to address the immediate stabilisation and recovery needs in geographical areas retaken from IS in Anbar, Ninewa, Salah-Din, Kirkuk and Diyala which allows for the sustainable return of internally displaced persons (IDPs).
The Funding Facility for Stabilization (FFS) is organised in windows that support four types of activities: 1) Public works and light infrastructure rehabilitation with focus on education, electricity, health, housing, roads and bridges, sewage and water; 2) Livelihood assistance including employment; 3) Capacity support including to municipalities; and 4) Peaceful communities through Social cohesion.
The intended outcome of the intervention is that people in Iraq, civil society and communities, particularly women, have improved capacity to lead, participate in and contribute to the design and delivery of equitable and responsive services, especially for the most vulnerable populations. The ouputs of the project are:
Output 1: Iraqi Government in newly liberated areas is supported to address immediate challenges for return of internally displaced persons.
1.1 Carry out local assessments to identify immediate stabilization needs
1.2 Rehabilitate priority light infrastructure in newly liberated areas (window 1)
1.3 Support immediate income generation opportunities (Window 2)
1.4. Capacity development of Government authorities to facilitate stabilization (Window 3)
1.5 Design and implement initiatives to promote social cohesion (window 4)
Output 2 High impact medium-sized infrastructure projects are rehabilitated to sustain stabilization gains (Funding Facility for Expanded Stabilization)
2.1 Rehabilitation of priority, medium-size infrastructure projects
Output 3: Exit Strategy is drafted in consultation with the Government of Iraq, for the liberated governorates.
3.1 Exit Strategy for post-funding facility stabilization and development work in the liberated governorates.
The goals of the Transit Strategy
In order to facilitate transition and exit of the FFS as a large scale facility to to contribute to Iraq's stabilisation efforts, a Transition Strategy has been developed and was adopted the FFS steering committee in the fall of 2022. The objectives of the Transitions Strategy complements the above FFS objectives and helps focusing efforts during the reming period of the FFS.
The main goal of the FFS Transition is to preserve and protect the achieved stabilisation gains implemented by FFS since its inception. To achieve this goal, FFS Transition Strategy should ideally aim to
i) contribute to the non-re-emergence of ISIL;
ii) ensure that the IDPs that returned do not undergo a secondary displacement;
iii) support sub-national institutional mechanisms and human capacities to ensure sustainability of basic services funded by the facility; and
iv) strengthen, when and to the extent possible, existing local institutions (private sector and communities) to implement post-stabilization activities.
The Transition will aim to have a local government attaining sufficient capacity, by end of 2023, to sustainably advance the well-being of its entire population, including the reintegration of IDP's, through continuing stabilisation activities, even in the face of shocks and shifting targets.
To this end, the proposed aim of FFS Transition is to improve the capacity of the local government, by the end of 2023, to:
i) sustainably provide resilient basic services, ii) create jobs, and iii) enhance social cohesion.
Update 2023-09-15: Sida's additional support to 'Community Reconciliation and Reintegration of Iraqis Returning from Syrias Al-Hol camp' (FFS window 4):
The overall Objective: Iraqi nationals returning from Northeast Syria (NES), including those perceived to be formerly associated with the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL) who have been cleared by authorities are sustainably reintegrated back into communities, and community members live freely and peacefully and are involved in the social and economic life of the communities.
Output 1: An enabling environment for the return and reintegration of Iraqi nationals from Al-Hol Camp in NES is created.
Output 2: Iraqi nationals returning from Al-Hol Camp in NES, as well as community members in areas of return receive socio-economic reintegration support.
Output 3: Ensure the explosive ordnance contamination in the targeted areas is mapped and no longer poses a threat to the returning IDPs.
